details:
Ember Protocol

The Lost Machines. The Forgotten Missions. The Evidence That Remains.

Project Overview

Ember Protocol is an interactive space-exploration and science-learning game inspired by real NASA missions and the abandoned equipment left behind during decades of space exploration. It transforms historical spacecraft, planetary missions, and scientific discoveries into an immersive experience where players investigate forgotten technologies, solve scientific challenges, and uncover the stories behind humanity's exploration of space.

The game takes players across four major worlds: the Moon, Mars, Deep Space, and The Convergence. Through a series of missions, players explore abandoned spacecraft and scientific equipment, inspect their components, recover historical evidence, and complete challenges based on real space science.

How Does It Work?

Players begin in a futuristic archive where they select worlds and missions. Each mission combines exploration, investigation, and problem-solving.

  • 2D Ground Archive: Players explore environments, interact with archive terminals, discover historical records, and receive transmissions that reveal mission stories.
  • 3D Spacecraft Inspection: Players examine interactive 3D models of spacecraft, landers, rovers, and scientific instruments. Hotspots reveal the purpose and engineering behind individual components.
  • Scientific Challenges: Players solve puzzles involving spacecraft communication, gravity assists, planetary exploration, orbital mechanics, and scientific observations.
  • Shuttle Flight Simulator: Players experience space navigation through a simulator featuring telemetry, throttle control, camera views, and celestial navigation.
  • Evidence Vault and Timeline: Players collect evidence and connect discoveries across different missions and historical periods.

The campaign is designed around 24 missions across four worlds, gradually connecting individual discoveries into a larger scientific story.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Ember Protocol aims to make space science more accessible, engaging, and understandable, especially for young learners.

  1. STEM Education: Introduces astronomy, physics, robotics, engineering, and planetary science through interactive challenges.
  2. Learning Through Exploration: Encourages players to investigate how real spacecraft worked instead of simply reading about them.
  3. Historical Preservation: Brings attention to forgotten and abandoned space hardware and the scientific achievements associated with it.
  4. Critical Thinking: Challenges players to interpret evidence, understand scientific principles, and solve problems.
  5. Inspiration for Future Innovators: Encourages young people to explore space science, engineering, and technology.

The project does not require specialized physical hardware; it is designed to be experienced through a standard computer.

What Makes the Project Creative?

The creative aspect of Ember Protocol is its combination of historical space exploration, interactive investigation, scientific puzzles, and immersive gameplay.

Instead of presenting NASA missions as static educational content, the game turns abandoned spacecraft into explorable environments and scientific evidence into playable challenges. Players can inspect spacecraft components, investigate their engineering purposes, and solve problems inspired by the actual technologies and discoveries of those missions.

It also combines multiple gameplay styles—2D exploration, 3D inspection, scientific puzzles, and a shuttle simulator—within one connected campaign. This creates a learning experience where scientific knowledge is discovered through gameplay rather than delivered only through text.

Factors Considered During Development

The team considered several important factors:

  • Scientific Accuracy: Using NASA and JPL resources to ground spacecraft models, mission histories, and scientific challenges in real exploration.
  • Educational Value: Ensuring that each mission teaches a meaningful scientific or engineering concept.
  • Accessibility: Making complex scientific ideas understandable through visual explanations and interactive activities.
  • Engagement: Combining different gameplay mechanics to maintain player interest.
  • Historical Context: Respecting the real achievements, limitations, and stories behind each mission.
  • Technical Feasibility: Considering performance, 3D asset complexity, rendering requirements, and the ability to run the experience on standard computers.
  • Scalability: Structuring the campaign so that additional missions, spacecraft, and scientific challenges can be introduced in the future.

Campaign Sector: 4 Worlds & 24 Levels

🌕 WORLD 1: THE MOON (7 Levels)

  1. M1: A Photograph Before Touchdown (Ranger 7) — Camera & Impact Telemetry
  2. M2: Surveyor's Soft Landing (Surveyor 1) — Landing Radar & Retro-Rockets
  3. M3: Eagle's Quiet Workshop (Apollo 11 Eagle) — Lunar Module & EASEP
  4. M4: The Rover Track Cipher (Apollo 15-17 LRV) — Electric Rover & Route Map
  5. M5: Seismometer Aftershock (Apollo ALSEP) — Seismometer & Waveform Filter
  6. M6: The Shadowed Crater (LCROSS & Lunar Prospector) — Spectrometer & Plume
  7. M7: Ebb, Flow, and the Final Key (GRAIL & LADEE) — Gravity Map & 3D Orbiter

🔴 WORLD 2: MARS (7 Levels)

  1. R1: Viking's First Surface Report (Viking 1 & 2) — Soil Lab & Weather Station
  2. R2: Sojourner's Command Queue (Pathfinder & Sojourner) — Rocker-Bogie & Command Queue
  3. R3: The Troy Soft-Soil Case (Spirit (MER-A)) — Wheel-Slip & Current Diagnostics
  4. R4: Opportunity's Water Clue (Opportunity (MER-B)) — Solar Graph & Mineral Cards
  5. R5: Phoenix Under the Surface (Phoenix Lander) — Robotic Arm & Subsurface Ice
  6. R6: The Landing That Went Silent (Mars Polar Lander) — EDL Timeline & Fault Tree
  7. R7: Ingenuity: Flight in Thin Air (Ingenuity & Perseverance) — 3D Rotor & Sky Crane Debris

🌌 WORLD 3: DEEP SPACE (7 Levels)

  1. D1: Pioneer's Last Packet (Pioneer 10) — High-Gain Antenna & RTG Power
  2. D2: Deep Space 1: Ion Engine Trial (Deep Space 1) — Ion Engine & Thrust Planner
  3. D3: Kepler's Missing Dip (Kepler Telescope) — Photometer & Light Curve
  4. D4: Spitzer's Invisible Heat (Spitzer Telescope) — Infrared Detector & Wavelengths
  5. D5: The Gravity of Eros (NEAR Shoemaker) — 433 Eros 3D Shape & Low-G Nav
  6. D6: Deep Impact: Read the Plume (Deep Impact) — Kinetic Impactor & Plume Spectrum
  7. D7: The Human Discovery Signal (Golden Records) — Open-Source Rover CAD & Pulsar Map

⚡ WORLD 4: THE CONVERGENCE (3 Climax Finale Levels)

  1. 4.1: The Three-World Black Box (LCROSS, Opportunity, Pioneer 10) — Cross-planetary data correlation
  2. 4.2: The Impossible Explorer — Modular 3D CAD & Fault Simulation across vacuum, heat, and thin air
  3. 4.3: Last Light of Humanity — Full Synthesis & Node Blueprint master planetary override signal

2D Archive Exploration (Scenes 1 & 2)

  • Full-Bleed Cover Scaling: Custom canvas renderer guaranteeing zero letterbox borders on any aspect ratio or device size.
  • Scene 1 (Outside Archive): Side-scrolling launch complex exterior (assets/images/bg.jpeg), animated 4-frame avatar walk cycles, jumping, sprinting, reaching the NASA Archive Gate with popup entry dialogs.
  • Scene 2 (Archive Facility): High-tech subterranean facility (assets/images/2nd.png), glowing CRT computer desk (assets/images/computer_desk.png), and exit doorway back to the launch site.
  • TULIP Terminal Dialogs: Sequential typed emergency broadcast transmissions (Transmissions 1 to 3) with indicator dots and mission launch hooks.
  • Temporal Trajectory Warp: Animated year-counter countdown (2027 ➔ 2030 ➔ 2034 ➔ 2038 ➔ 2042 ➔ 2045 ➔ 2047) with real-time status telemetry before transitioning into space!

Interactive 3D Spacecraft Inspection & Planetary Missions

  • 10 NASA Missions & Destinies:
    1. Mission 01 — First Signal: Pioneer 10 Interstellar Probe (Jupiter flyby, RTG power, Golden Plaque).
    2. Mission 02 — The Lunar Archive: Apollo Lunar Module (Eagle), Tranquility Base, EASEP seismic instruments, LADEE.
    3. Mission 03 — The Asteroid Frontier: Dawn Ion Propulsion Spacecraft, Vesta, Ceres, bright faculae.
    4. Mission 04 — The Red Planet: Opportunity Rover, Viking Lander, and Ingenuity Helicopter.
    5. Mission 05 — The Exoplanet Observatory: Kepler Space Telescope & Spitzer, transit photometry.
    6. Mission 06 — The Asteroid Frontier II: Occator Crater sodium carbonate salts and GRaND water-ice mapping.
    7. Mission 07 — The Exoplanet Hunter: Kepler-186f Earth-size world and statistical planetary abundance laws.
    8. Mission 08 — The Lunar Atmosphere: LADEE dust levitation and exosphere analysis.
    9. Mission 09 — Aerial Flight on Mars: Ingenuity Helicopter 72 historic sorties in 1% atmosphere.
    10. Mission 10 — The Reusable Fleet: Space Shuttle Orbiter, SSME main engines, and silica thermal tiles.
  • 3D Touch Orbit Controls: Drag across the screen to rotate spacecraft 360° horizontally and vertically.
  • Interactive Hotspot Beacons: Tap glowing beacons on antennas, thrusters, and instruments to inspect telemetry specifications and launch recovery puzzles.

Ultimately, Ember Protocol turns forgotten space technology into an interactive gateway to scientific discovery. It reminds players that abandoned machines are not simply remnants of the past—they are evidence of humanity's curiosity, engineering, and determination to explore the unknown.

Our goal is not to create a simulation or game that merely runs on a limited range of devices. Instead, we prioritize *accessibility and compatibility over performance, ensuring that the application runs smoothly across a wide range of Android devices. We have also optimized and compressed the entire app bundle to **under 50 MB*, making it lightweight, accessible, and easy to install.
